primary_citation: 18 U.S.C. §1030 (Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, Pub. L. 98-473 (1984); amended through Pub. L. 110-326 (2008))
short_title: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act — Unauthorized Access to Protected Computers; Civil Remedy
one_line_rule: Intentional unauthorized access to a computer affecting interstate commerce, causing $5,000+ loss, is actionable in a civil suit for compensatory damages and injunctive relief; using another's credentials without authorization is 'without authorization' regardless of Van Buren.

case_law.cite: Van Buren v. United States, 593 U.S. 374 (2021)
case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: 'Exceeds authorized access' is scope-based: accessing files/systems outside permission scope; NOT purpose-based misuse of authorized access. 'Without authorization' prong unaffected — SIM swap attackers still liable.

case_law.cite: United States v. Nosal, 676 F.3d 854 (9th Cir. 2012) (en banc) (Nosal I); 844 F.3d 1024 (9th Cir. 2016) (Nosal II)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: Nosal I: scope-based 'exceeds authorized access' (adopted by Van Buren). Nosal II: credential-sharing to grant unauthorized user access = 'without authorization'; SIM swap attacker using hijacked phone number = 'without authorization' under Nosal II.

sim_swap_application.theory: §1030(a)(2) 'without authorization': attacker used hijacked phone number (SIM swap) to access Michael's accounts — email, SSA portal, TreasuryDirect, financial accounts — with no authorization
sim_swap_application.civil_track: §1030(g): $5,000 loss threshold met by aggregated account access response costs + benefit denial + remediation
sim_swap_application.$5000_basis: SSA disability denial (monthly benefits × months denied) + communications security costs + identity remediation
sim_swap_application.rico_predicate: §1030(a)(4) computer fraud = RICO predicate; multi-year campaign = H.J. Inc. pattern
sim_swap_application.defendant: Ryan McClaran (SIM swap orchestrator) as primary §1030 defendant; AT&T negligence theory runs on separate tort track
sim_swap_application.sol: 2 years from discovery; each unauthorized access is a fresh violation; continuing campaign = rolling SOL
